title: Load each scanned parcel once

blocks.text: At the sorting hub, every parcel passes two scanners, and a jam sends some parcels past the same scanner again a few minutes later. The loading list is supposed to hold each parcel once, but the drivers' lists have started showing the same parcel two or three times, and the loaders put it on the truck that many times in their count.
`HubScans.loadingList(...)` already reads the scanner lines into `Parcel`s. Finish the three `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/HubScans.java`:

items: `Parcel.equals(...)` and `Parcel.hashCode()`: a parcel is identified by its carrier and its tracking number; the scan time is not part of what it is;
`unique(...)`: each parcel once, as it was first scanned, in the order of the scans.

blocks.text: Keep `Parcel` a class. About six lines in total.

cases.says: scans of different parcels are all on the loading list
two scans of one parcel, read from two scanner lines, are equal; a different carrier makes a different parcel
two identical scans of one parcel give one entry on the loading list
a parcel scanned again later is still one parcel, and the entry kept is its first scan
the loading list is in the order the parcels were first scanned

origin.section: distinct Uses equals and hashCode, So a Class Without Both Keeps Every Copy

concepts: distinct keeps every copy of a class without equals and hashCode, or with equals alone, and the fields in equals decide which copy, the first in encounter order, survives.
